text: At 3:09 a.m., the correlation rule finds a match it's never surfaced before. The firewall allows 203.0.114.77 through to the admin jump host on RDP. Five minutes later, that same address signs in to Entra ID as n.pettit@hartwellru.com.

Mara opens the runbook and starts at Triage. Is n.pettit's 3 a.m. activity expected? No. Is 203.0.114.77 a recognized address? No. Is this account in the Conditional Access pilot yet? No -- so only a password was required. Did the sign-in succeed? Yes.
Every one of those checks points the same direction. Mara escalates past Triage, logs it as a real concern, and moves into Scope -- checking what else this account or address touches.
Triage did its job: it turned a raw alert into a confirmed, documented concern. What it hasn't answered is how 203.0.114.77 was allowed through the firewall in the first place.
The correlation rule caught the symptom. It didn't explain the cause. That's where the investigation goes next.
